recipes.name: Chicken Tinga Bowls
steps: Sauté sliced onion in a little oil until soft, about 5 min. Add garlic, cumin, and oregano, cook 1 min.
Add crushed tomatoes, chipotle peppers, and chicken thighs. Cover and simmer 25 min until chicken is cooked through.
Remove chicken and shred with two forks. Return to sauce and simmer uncovered 5 min to thicken.
Cook cauliflower rice in a dry pan 4–5 min. Season with salt and lime juice.
Warm black beans. Assemble bowls: cauliflower rice → black beans → tinga chicken → yogurt crema → cilantro + lime.
recipes.tips: Chipotle gives big smoky flavor in small portions. Cauliflower rice keeps carbs low without feeling like a sacrifice.

recipes.name: Vegetarian Tinga Bowls

ingredients.name: Young green jackfruit in brine (canned, drained)

steps: Sauté sliced onion until soft. Add garlic, cumin, and oregano, cook 1 min.
Add torn mushrooms and cook until they release liquid and begin to brown, about 8 min.
Add drained shredded jackfruit, crushed tomatoes, and chipotle peppers. Simmer 20 min, shredding jackfruit with a fork as it softens.
Cook cauliflower rice in a dry pan. Warm black beans.
Assemble bowls same as Chicken Tinga.
recipes.tips: Jackfruit mimics pulled meat texture beautifully. Mushrooms add umami depth so you won't miss the chicken.

recipes.name: Carne Asada Pepper Bowl
steps: Marinate flank steak in lime juice, orange juice, garlic, cumin, and smoked paprika for at least 1 hour (overnight is better).
Toss sliced poblanos, red onion, and bell peppers in olive oil. Roast at 425°F for 25 min until charred at the edges.
Grill or sear steak over very high heat, 3–4 min per side for medium. Rest 5 min, then slice thinly against the grain.
Serve over brown rice with roasted peppers, sliced avocado, and fresh pico de gallo.
recipes.tips: Slice the steak thin against the grain — it feels like more food visually. A good char on the peppers is key to the flavor.

recipes.name: Vegetarian Carne Asada Bowl
steps: Cut cauliflower into thick steaks. Marinate in lime juice, orange juice, garlic, cumin, smoked paprika, and chili powder for 30 min.
Roast cauliflower at 425°F for 30–35 min, flipping once, until charred and tender.
Roast sliced peppers and onion alongside. Warm black beans.
Serve over brown rice with roasted vegetables, sliced avocado, and pico de gallo.
recipes.tips: A very hot oven is essential — the char on the cauliflower is where all the flavor comes from.

recipes.name: Saag Chicken
steps: Blend or finely chop spinach and set aside.
Heat ghee. Sauté onion until golden, about 8 min. Add garlic and ginger, cook 2 min.
Add cumin, coriander, turmeric, garam masala, and chili powder. Stir 1 min. Add diced tomatoes and cook until sauce thickens, about 5 min.
Add cubed chicken breast and cook through, 8–10 min.
Stir in spinach and simmer 5 min. Remove from heat and stir in Greek yogurt.
Serve with cauliflower rice or a small portion of naan.
recipes.tips: Spinach is extremely volume-efficient — 500g cooks down to almost nothing but keeps you full. Greek yogurt adds creaminess without heavy cream.

recipes.name: Saag Paneer
steps: Cut paneer into cubes and pan-fry in ghee until golden on each side. Set aside.
In the same pan, sauté onion until golden. Add garlic, ginger, and all spices, cook 2 min.
Add diced tomatoes and cook until oil separates from the sauce, about 5 min.
Add spinach and simmer 5 min until wilted. Stir in Greek yogurt.
Fold in the pan-fried paneer gently. Simmer 3 min and serve.
recipes.tips: Pan-frying paneer first gives it a golden crust that holds up in the sauce. Don't skip this step.

recipes.name: Dal Makhani

ingredients.name: Whole black lentils (urad dal), soaked overnight
Plain Greek yogurt or light cream

steps: Soak black lentils overnight. Drain and rinse.
Simmer lentils in fresh water until very soft, about 45–60 min on stovetop (20 min in pressure cooker).
Sauté onion in butter until deep golden. Add garlic, ginger, and spices, cook 2 min.
Add crushed tomatoes and cook until the oil separates, about 8 min.
Add cooked lentils, kidney beans, and 200ml water. Simmer 20 min, stirring occasionally.
Stir in Greek yogurt or cream. Adjust seasoning and serve.
recipes.tips: Urad dal is one of the highest-fiber legumes — a 200g portion is extremely filling. Better the next day after the flavors meld.

recipes.name: Ginger Beef Broccoli Stir Fry
steps: Mix soy sauce, oyster sauce, rice vinegar, ginger, garlic, sesame oil, and cornstarch into a sauce. Toss sliced beef in half and marinate 15 min.
Blanch broccoli florets in boiling water for 2 min. Drain.
Sear beef in a very hot wok in batches, 1–2 min per batch. Remove and set aside.
Stir fry broccoli, snap peas, and bell pepper 3–4 min until tender-crisp.
Return beef to the wok, add remaining sauce. Toss 1 min until sauce coats everything.
Serve over brown rice.
recipes.tips: Sear beef in small batches — overcrowding steams instead of sears. A hot wok makes all the difference.

recipes.name: Ginger Tofu Broccoli Stir Fry
steps: Press tofu well for at least 20 min (wrap in a clean towel with something heavy on top). Cut into cubes.
Toss tofu in half the sauce mixture. Bake at 400°F for 25 min, flipping halfway, until golden and slightly crisp.
Blanch broccoli 2 min. Stir fry vegetables in a hot wok 3–4 min.
Add baked tofu and remaining sauce. Toss 1 min.
Serve over brown rice and top with sesame seeds.
recipes.tips: Pressing tofu is essential — moisture is the enemy of a good sear. Baking instead of frying gives a meatier texture with less oil.

recipes.name: Kung Pao Chicken
steps: Mix sauce: soy sauce, rice vinegar, hoisin, sesame oil, cornstarch, and 2 tbsp water.
Toss cubed chicken in 1 tbsp soy sauce and a little cornstarch. Sear in a hot wok until cooked through, about 6 min. Remove.
Stir fry dried chilies and minced garlic in sesame oil for 30 seconds.
Add zucchini, celery, and bell pepper. Cook 3–4 min until tender-crisp.
Return chicken to wok. Add sauce and roasted peanuts. Toss 1–2 min until sauce thickens.
Serve over brown rice.
recipes.tips: Peanuts add satisfying fat and crunch — a small amount goes a long way. Zucchini adds bulk with almost no calories.

recipes.name: Kung Pao Tofu
steps: Press and cube tofu. Bake at 400°F for 25 min until golden and crisp.
Mix sauce: soy sauce, hoisin, rice vinegar, sesame oil, cornstarch, and 2 tbsp water.
Stir fry dried chilies and garlic in sesame oil 30 seconds.
Add zucchini, celery, bell pepper, and edamame. Cook 3–4 min.
Add baked tofu and sauce. Toss 1–2 min. Top with sesame seeds.
Serve over brown rice.
recipes.tips: Edamame adds a meaningful protein boost. Baking the tofu ahead of time means faster stir fry assembly.

recipes.name: Grilled Salmon with Lentil Tabbouleh
steps: Season salmon with salt, pepper, and a drizzle of olive oil.
Grill salmon 4–5 min per side until cooked through. Rest 2 min.
Cook lentils in salted water until tender, about 20 minutes. Drain and cool completely.
Combine cooled lentils with diced cucumber, tomato, parsley, mint, lemon juice, and olive oil.
Serve salmon over tabbouleh.
recipes.tips: Swap salmon for chicken breast for a lower-fat version. Lentils can be made a day ahead and refrigerated.

recipes.name: Turkey-Stuffed Bell Peppers
steps: Preheat oven to 375°F. Cut tops off peppers and remove seeds.
Brown ground turkey with onion, garlic, and Italian seasoning.
Mix in cooked rice, diced tomatoes, and tomato paste. Season to taste.
Stuff peppers with turkey mixture and place in a baking dish.
Top with shredded mozzarella. Bake 30–35 min until peppers are tender.
recipes.tips: Use cauliflower rice instead of white rice to reduce carbs significantly. These reheat well the next day.

recipes.name: Shrimp + Edamame Stir-Fry with Brown Rice
steps: Cook brown rice per package directions.
Heat sesame oil in a wok over high heat until smoking.
Stir-fry shrimp 2–3 min until pink. Remove and set aside.
Add edamame, snap peas, and bell pepper. Stir-fry 3–4 min.
Return shrimp to wok. Add soy sauce, ginger, and garlic. Toss to coat for 1 min.
Serve over brown rice.
recipes.tips: Frozen shrimp work great — thaw in cold water for 10 min. Edamame is a GLP-1 MVP for protein + fiber.

recipes.name: White Bean + Tuna Salad with Lemon Vinaigrette
steps: Drain and rinse white beans and tuna.
Whisk together lemon juice, olive oil, Dijon, garlic, salt, and pepper.
Combine beans, tuna, arugula, red onion, and capers in a large bowl.
Drizzle with vinaigrette and toss gently.
Serve immediately or refrigerate up to 2 days.
recipes.tips: No-cook meal — great for days when appetite is low. High fiber keeps you full longer.

recipes.name: Spiced Chickpea + Chicken Thigh Skillet
steps: Season chicken thighs with cumin, smoked paprika, coriander, salt, and pepper.
Sear chicken in olive oil 4–5 min per side until golden. Remove from pan.
Sauté onion and garlic in the same pan until softened, about 4 min.
Add chickpeas, diced tomatoes, and chicken broth. Stir to combine.
Return chicken to pan. Simmer 15–20 min until cooked through.
Finish with fresh cilantro and a squeeze of lemon.
recipes.tips: Chicken thighs stay moist even when appetite is suppressed. One-pan cleanup makes this ideal for low-energy days.
